subject: Mutual Action Plan: Capacity onramp & contingency (Dedicated → Private transition)
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@medilabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Mutual Action Plan: Capacity onramp & contingency (Dedicated → Private transition)

Hi Elena / Raj —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our follow-up, I put together an initial mutual action plan (attached: MAP_v1.xlsx) that lays out the evaluation milestones, acceptance criteria, and the capacity reservation timeline if MediLabs moves forward with Dedicated capacity and later transitions to Private (VPC / on-prem). High-level notes below — please review and let me know gaps.

Key assumptions (please confirm):
- Primary workload: low-latency chat + bulk embeddings for search.
- Target tps: 120 qps sustained at 128-token average response; peak bursts to 450 qps.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 300ms for generation.

Recommended starting sizing (open to iterate):
- Dedicated staging pool: 16 GPUs (A100-equivalent) for PoC (throughput testing + acceptance).
- Dedicated production pool (initial): 64 GPUs (A100-equivalent) with 2x burst lane (up to 128 for short windows).
- Private/on-prem target pool: 64–96 GPUs depending on final model choice and compression.

Lead-time guidance (approx):
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed): allocation & scheduling 6–10 weeks from signed reservation (depends on tranche availability).
- Private (on-prem procurement + network + KMS): 12–20 weeks (hardware lead times + install + validation).

Minimal acceptance criteria for MAP gate (Eval → Commit):
1) End-to-end p95 latency validated in staging at 80% of target load.
2) Cost-per-1M tokens under agreed budget band (see RL-estimate-q4.pdf).
3) Security checklist: SOC2 artifacts supplied + network test plan completed.

Action items proposed (owner / target):
- Redwood: produce a configuration-level capacity-sizer and cost estimate (attachment: capacity-sizer.xlsx) — Ben / Karthik — due Wed 2027-01-06.
- MediLabs: finalize expected qps/workload mix and internal procurement lead time for on-prem — Elena / Raj — due Fri 2027-01-08.
- Both: sign MAP v1 and agree on PoC window (2–3 weeks) — target signature by 2027-01-12 (DocuSign link included).

Open questions for your team:
1) Can you confirm preferred region for Dedicated (us-west/us-east/eu)?
2) Any procurement constraints (purchase order cycles, vendor approval timelines) we should slot into the MAP?

Next steps: if the assumptions look good, I’ll lock the MAP into HubSpot and schedule a 30-min handshake call to align on PoC test plan next week.

Thanks —
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jasmine@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

Attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx; capacity-sizer.xlsx; RL-estimate-q4.pdf

From: Elena Soto <elena@medilabs.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@medilabs.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Dec 2026 11:09:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: Capacity onramp & contingency (Dedicated → Private transition)

Jasmine — thanks, this is clear and helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Region: we prefer us-east for data residency and colocation benefits.
- Procurement: our PO cycle is monthly but approvals for new vendors can take 6–8 weeks; hardware budgeting for on-prem typically hits the next fiscal quarter (starts Mar 1).
- Workload: the 120 qps number is accurate for steady-state; embedding batch jobs run overnight and could spike token consumption but not latency-sensitive.

Questions: 
1) Is there a way to stage with a smaller Dedicated pool and rely on temporary burst lanes while procurement occurs? We want to keep committed spend conservative during Q1.
2) Can Redwood provide an option to start with mixed instance types (e.g., partial H100 + A100-equivalent) to reduce immediate lead time / cost?

I’ll coordinate with procurement and get back on vendor approval timing by Fri. If you can update the MAP with us-east region and a conservative cost band, that would help our finance review.

—Elena
Elena Soto
VP Product & ML Engineering | MediLabs
elena@medilabs.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Soto <elena@medilabs.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@medilabs.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Dec 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: Capacity onramp & contingency (Dedicated → Private transition)

Thanks — quick technical note to help scope capacity and the PoC: 

1) Mixed-instance staging: yes — we can provision a hybrid pool for the PoC. Recommendation: 12 GPUs H100-equivalent (for low-latency model variants) + 8 A100-equivalent (for cost-sensitive background workloads). That gets you realistic latency measurements while reducing immediate allocation.

2) Model variants & cache: if MediLabs is open to a quantized 8-bit production variant + active prefix/KV caching for chat, we estimate a 30–40% reduction in GPU count for steady state. I’ve encoded these knobs into capacity-sizer.xlsx (tab: "variants").

3) Acceptance test plan (PoC):
- Day 1: baseline throughput with current model on small sample corpus.
- Day 3: p95 latency validation at 80% of target sustained qps.
- Day 5: failover & fallback test (simulate 30% traffic reroute to smaller quantized model).

4) Lead-time clarification: Dedicated allocation can often be completed in 4–8 weeks if mixing instance pools and taking burst lanes; the 6–10 week window Jasmine cited is conservative. Private on-prem procurement still sits at 12–20 weeks.

I’ll add a short appendix with trade-offs and updated sizing ranges to the MAP in Drive. Ben — can you update the cost sheet and produce an incremental PO-friendly summary for procurement?

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Architect, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena@medilabs.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@medilabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Jan 2027 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Mutual Action Plan: Capacity onramp & contingency (Dedicated → Private transition)

Elena / Raj —

Great — thanks for the quick responses and the procurement context. I updated the MAP to reflect us-east preference, added a conservative staging path (hybrid pool) and included Karthik's reduced-count variant scenarios. Ben attached an interim PO summary and a conservative cost band for Q1 spend.

Next mutual action items (finalized):
- Redwood (Ben): PO summary & Q1 cost guardrails (attachment: RL-estimate-q4.pdf) — due 2027-01-06.
- MediLabs (Elena): procurement approval window & internal PO owner — due 2027-01-08.
- Both: sign MAP_v1 (DocuSign); target signature by 2027-01-12 to secure tranche scheduling.

Contingency & fallbacks: if on-prem procurement misses the Q1 window, we recommend a staggered commit: 30% initial Dedicated commit for 3 months, incremental top-ups on 60-day cadence to reach target pool without long upfront spend. This is in the MAP (tab: "staggered-commit").

Please reply with "ack - MAP_v1" to indicate alignment, or propose edits inline in the Drive doc. I’ll schedule the handshake call once we have acknowledgements.

Best —
Jasmine

Onward —
Attachments: MAP_v1.xlsx; RL-estimate-q4.pdf; capacity-sizer.xlsx
